title: Working with Python Lists
description: Build and update an ordered collection by managing a simple packing list in Python.
learning_objectives: Create a Python list containing three items.
Use zero-based indexing to retrieve a specific item.
Use append and pop to add and remove an item at the end of a list.

slides.title: Create your packing list
slides.content: Write items = ['map', 'bottle', 'jacket']. Square brackets create a list, and commas separate its three items. Python preserves the order you wrote.
slides.key_takeaway: Use square brackets to create an ordered collection.

slides.title: Retrieve one item by position
slides.content: Evaluate items[0] to retrieve 'map'. Python starts counting at zero, so items[2] retrieves the third item, 'jacket'.
slides.key_takeaway: The index of the first item is zero.

slides.title: Add an item at the end
slides.content: Run items.append('snack'). The list now holds ['map', 'bottle', 'jacket', 'snack']. The three original items keep their positions.
slides.key_takeaway: append adds one item to the end of the existing list.

slides.title: Remove and inspect the last item
slides.content: Run removed = items.pop(). The list returns to its original three items, and removed holds the string 'snack'.
slides.key_takeaway: pop() removes and returns the last item when no index is supplied.

quiz.question: Your packing list is ['map', 'bottle', 'jacket']. Which expression retrieves 'bottle'?
quiz.explanation: The bottle is the second item, so its zero-based index is 1.

quiz.question: You append 'snack' to ['map', 'bottle', 'jacket']. What is now at index 2?
quiz.explanation: Appending places the snack at the end. The jacket keeps its original index of 2.

quiz.question: Your list ends with 'snack'. Which line removes that item and saves it for later?
quiz.explanation: With no index, pop removes the final item and returns it. The assignment saves that returned value.
